unit.title: Influence, community and social listening
unit.description: Influencer tiers, engagement, briefs and contracts, employee advocacy, community, social listening, brand lift

cards.definition: The document that frames a collaboration: goal, key message, mandatory mentions, dos and donts, deliverables, dates, usage rights and how results are measured. It leaves room for the creator voice.
cards.example: Two Reels and three stories, one promo code, the Collaboration commerciale mention, rights to reuse in ads for 3 months.

cards.definition: Choosing creators on audience match (age, country, interests), engagement quality and values, not on follower count. Fake followers and bought engagement are common; check audience data.
cards.example: A 30,000 follower cooking creator with 80 percent French followers beats a 500,000 lifestyle account with 70 percent abroad.

cards.definition: Content created by customers or paid creators in a customer style: reviews, unboxings, tutorials. It feels authentic and often outperforms polished ads on social platforms.
cards.example: A shampoo brand running ads made of short videos filmed by real users in their bathroom.

exercises.prompt: A creator has 40,000 very engaged followers. In the usual tiers, which category is it?
choices: Micro-influencer
Mega-influencer
Macro-influencer
Celebrity
exercises.explain: Common convention: nano under 10k, micro 10k to 100k, then mid, macro and mega. Thresholds vary by agency.

exercises.prompt: How do you choose between two creators for a French cosmetics launch?
choices: Audience in France, engagement quality, brand fit
Only the total number of followers they have
The price per post: the cheapest one wins
Whoever answers the first email the fastest
exercises.explain: Reach is worthless if the audience is abroad or fake. Ask for audience statistics and check comments.

exercises.prompt: A post is seen by 2,000 people and gets 100 interactions. What is the engagement rate per reach?
choices: 5 percent
2 percent
20 percent
50 percent
exercises.explain: 100 divided by 2,000. Rate per reach is fairer than per follower, since most followers never see a given post.

exercises.prompt: What should an influencer brief always include?
choices: Goal, key message, mandatory mentions, deliverables, rights
The exact script, word for word, to read
Only the date and the price of the post
The password of the brand account
exercises.explain: A good brief frames without killing the creator voice. Usage rights avoid disputes when you reuse content in ads.

choices: Monitoring what people say about you and your market online
Reading only the comments under your own posts
Buying followers to look more popular
Listening to podcasts about social media
exercises.explain: Listening covers brand, competitors and topics, even without tags. It feeds product, crisis management and content ideas.

exercises.prompt: Employees sharing company news on their own LinkedIn often reach more people than the company page.
exercises.explain: True. Personal profiles usually get more reach and trust than brand pages. Advocacy must stay voluntary and authentic.

exercises.prompt: How can you measure whether a video campaign changed brand perception?
choices: A brand lift study with exposed and control groups
Counting the likes on the video
The number of comments in one day
The cost per thousand impressions
exercises.explain: Brand lift compares awareness or consideration between people who saw the ads and a control group.

exercises.prompt: A customer complains loudly in the comments. Best first move?
choices: Answer quickly and publicly, then solve it in private
Delete the comment and block the person
Ignore it so it is buried by new posts
Reply with a joke to lighten things up
exercises.explain: Others read your answer. A fast, human, public reply plus a private fix often turns a critic into a fan.

exercises.prompt: Why do UGC-style ads often beat polished studio ads on TikTok?
choices: They look native to the feed and feel authentic
They are always cheaper to buy as media
The platform forbids studio videos
They never need a hook in the first seconds
exercises.explain: Ads that look like the content around them get watched. They still need a strong hook and a clear offer.

exercises.prompt: Put an influencer campaign in order.
steps: Set the goal and the measure of success
Shortlist creators on audience data and fit
Send the brief and sign the contract with rights
Validate content and check the legal mentions
Publish, track codes and links, and report results
exercises.explain: Goal first, then fit, a clear contract, a compliance check, and measurement with codes or tracked links.
